title: Lua Scripting in Redis
description: Use Lua scripts to run atomic logic directly inside Redis, reducing round trips and eliminating race conditions.

data.text: Redis supports executing Lua scripts via the EVAL command. When Redis receives a script, it loads, compiles, and caches it inside the server process. Subsequent executions of the same script run from the cache, so there is no repeated compilation overhead. More importantly, Redis treats the entire script as an atomic unit: no other command can interleave while the script is running.

This atomic guarantee is what makes Lua scripts powerful. Imagine a rate limiter that must check a counter, increment it, and decide whether to allow a request — all in one indivisible step. With individual Redis commands, a second client could slip between your GET and SET. With Lua, the check and update happen together without interruption.

data.text: Every script you send to EVAL is stored in Redis with a SHA1 hash. After the first execution, you can call the script again by its hash using EVALSHA. This avoids resending the full script body and is the preferred pattern in production. Most Redis clients manage EVALSHA transparently, falling back to EVAL only when the script is not yet cached.

data.title: Atomic rate limiter with Lua

data.text: In C#, you can load a Lua script once and reuse it. StackExchange.Redis supports Lua through the LoadLuaScript method, which returns a LuaScript object ready to execute. This avoids loading the same script repeatedly and keeps your code clean.

data.title: Lua script with StackExchange.Redis (C#)
Script Timeout
data.text: Redis kills Lua scripts that run longer than lua-time-limit (default 5 seconds). A slow script blocks all other commands. Keep scripts short, avoid unbounded loops, and do not perform blocking operations inside them.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Lua scripts execute atomically inside Redis
Scripts are cached by SHA1; EVALSHA avoids resending bodies
Use Lua for read-modify-write patterns that need atomicity
Keep scripts short to avoid hitting lua-time-limit
data.takeaway: Lua scripting turns Redis into a lightweight transaction engine. When you need atomic read-modify-write without the overhead of WATCH/MULTI/EXEC, a Lua script is usually the right tool.
